newsitem.title: UK: Lack of rain mars good UK grains crop outlook.
newsitem.headline: Lack of rain mars good UK grains crop outlook.

text.p: The the spring growing period is getting under way in the UK and cereals analysts are generally heartened by the state of crops.
But worries over the continued lack of rainfall remain.
"Things should start growing quite quickly now," one analyst said. "Crops look good. There's been no damage from the cold weather."
"We could do with a lot more rain," another said. "If it stays dry during March, people will start to get more worried," he said.
But the overall picture was not so bad, he said. One positive result of low rainfall levels was a high soil nitrogen content, which meant crops were green.

Poor conditions during January and February delayed spring barley sowing. "Drilling's been later than we'd have liked, after a shocking start to the year," he said. But now the delay was being made up. "People have been drilling like mad," he said.
"People are a bit worried about the low level of rainfall so far this year," one farming source in East Anglia said.
Their concerns centred on whether the dry start to the year might herald continued low rainfall, she said.
But there were also concerns about what it might mean for the availability of water for irrigation. "A lot of the light land depends on irrigation," she said.
